title: Pass through finite approximants for analytic infinite objects
obstacle: A formal coefficient or infinite expression needs an analytic integral/sum identity.
procedure: Prove the exact finite identity first.
Prove convergence in the mode required by the chosen integral/sum operation.
Pass to the limit and identify the stabilized coefficient or destination object.
verification: Record the majorant/uniform region and every sum-integral interchange.
positive_example: Theta polynomial coefficients pass to circle integrals using uniform-on-circle convergence.
negative_example: Pointwise convergence alone does not justify passing a circle integral through the limit.
version_boundary: Pattern observed in these pinned sources; exact APIs must be checked at application.

evidence.excerpt:
## Closure

The finite-product extension and uniform-on-circle limiting argument are now
compiled.  The declarations
`tendstoUniformlyOn_analyticThetaProduct`,
`tendsto_circleIntegral_analyticThetaProduct_div_pow`, and
`circleIntegral_analyticThetaProduct_div_pow` prove the exact statement

\[
 [z^n]\prod_{i=1}^d\Theta_i(z)
 = \frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{|z|=\rho}
 \frac{\prod_{i=1}^d\Theta_i(z)}{z^{n+1}}\,dz,
 \qquad 0<\rho<1,
\]

with the coefficient identified with the already formalized bilateral theta
coefficient.  The proof passes through the finite partial products and the
explicit uniform limit; it does not introduce an abstract analytic-function
axiom.
